chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Abu Amir, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The vinegar, when cooked until three and a half diwaniq are removed from it, then left until it cools, two-thirds of it has gone and one-third remains."

key_terms.الْعَصِيرُ: Vinegar (specifically grape vinegar, often discussed in fiqh regarding najasah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on vinegar that has been cooked until a certain amount evaporates?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the physical transformation of vinegar (*asir*) through boiling, a key indicator for its ritual purity (*taharah*) in Shia jurisprudence. By specifying the evaporation of three and a half *diwaniq* (a weight unit), the Imam establishes a tangible criterion for when the substance changes state, distinguishing it from its original form. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on empirical observation in determining the legal status of consumables.
